finding: A Git `ps` failure at the second read is swallowed, so kin's descendant walk can miss a Git Bash descendant of an orphan and agent-stop still answers `stopped: true`.
why: `_msys_children` turns the new `None` (ps failed) into `{}` via `or {}`, and `kin` calls `tree(orphan)` (line 320) after its own `_msys_parents()` read, so a ps failure or timeout in that later read drops every MSYS edge of the orphan's tree with no gap reported; the delta reports a failed ps only on the `_parent_ended` path.
fix: Have `_msys_children` return None (or raise) when `_msys_parents()` is None, and have `kin` read the process list and Git ps once and build the orphans' trees from that snapshot, adding a gap when a read fails.
evidence: +        for child, parent in (_msys_parents() or {}).items():   /   +    found = list(dict.fromkeys(m for orphan in found for m in tree(orphan) if m not in skip))

finding: No test fails if the `m not in skip` filter on an orphan's descendants is removed.
why: The filter is the only guard that keeps the caller, a tree member or an ancestor out of the kill list when `tree(orphan)` reaches one (on Windows an MSYS edge can do that). In every kin test an orphan's descendants (410, 450, 480) lie outside `skip`, so the mutant survives, and the dedup after it is also unchecked.
fix: Add a kin case in which `tree(orphan)` includes the caller or a member (for example an MSYS edge from an orphan to the caller) and assert that process is not in `found`; add one orphan reached twice to cover the dedup.
evidence: +    found = list(dict.fromkeys(m for orphan in found for m in tree(orphan) if m not in skip))

finding: The third re-run records V28 and Q20 as passed, but its own Codex evidence shows an orphan descendant (`cat.exe` 30548) still alive after `stopped` true, explained only by an unverified inference.
why: The agent-stop honesty bar is that `stopped: true` means no process of the agent survives; run4/after-cx.txt line 3 reads `alive 30548`, and run4/cat-cx-before.txt shows it was the orphan bash's child with a gone Windows parent, yet the paragraph says `most likely still shutting down (inferred, not verified on the pane run)`.
fix: Re-run the Codex pane case polling the process list until 30548 is gone, and record whether the sweep returned it; if it did not, record V28 as failed on that case and fix the walk, not the wording.
evidence: "the orphan's `cat.exe` was still listed by `tasklist` on that check and was gone from Git's `ps` seconds later" ... "(inferred, not verified on the pane run)"

finding: No test runs the new `_msys_parents` failure branches (non-zero exit, OSError) or the `_msys_children` fallback; the Windows kin test patches `_msys_parents` to return None directly.
why: The new lines 117-121 of process.py (`return None` on error, `if done.returncode != 0: return None`) can regress to the old `{}` answer, which treated every MSYS-less peer as an orphan to kill, and no test fails.
fix: Add a Windows test that patches `process._msys_ps` and `process.subprocess.run` to give a non-zero exit and an OSError and asserts `_msys_parents()` is None and `kin` names a gap.
evidence: +    msys: dict | None = {460: 10}   ...   +    monkeypatch.setattr(process, "_msys_parents", lambda: msys)   (the only test touching the None path)

finding: The delta's own motivating case, a Git Bash orphan that has MSYS children, has no automated test; the MSYS test still uses an orphan with no child.
why: The orphan there is the `sleep 611` itself, so the descendant walk through MSYS edges (`_msys_children` inside `tree(orphan)`) is exercised only by the manual live run; the generic NESTED test uses Windows parent edges only.
fix: Extend the MSYS test so the orphan is a `bash -c '(sleep N | cat) &'` shell and assert its `sleep` and `cat` children die.
evidence: inner = rf"sleep 611 & p=\$!; sleep 1; cat /proc/\$p/winpid > '{left.as_posix()}'"   (unchanged; the delta added no MSYS-with-children test)

finding: Possible variable double-duty: `ended` is a tri-state (True, False, None) and line 312 relies on truthiness to tell True from None.
why: A reader must recall that None means "could not read" and falls through to the unknown branch only because `born` is forced to None; the tri-state is easy to break in a later edit.
fix: Name the three cases (for example `if ended is None: unknown.append(...)` before the age check) instead of folding None into `born = None`.

finding: The no-process-list test leaves `_msys_parents` unpatched, so on Windows it runs Git's real `ps -e`.
why: `kin` reads `_msys_parents()` before the empty-list check, so the test depends on the host's Git install and costs a real subprocess, which the neighbouring kin tests avoid by patching it.
evidence:
